tasks.instruction: Wykorzystując podane słowa (wyróżnione pogrubionym drukiem), należy uzupełnić luki w zdaniach tak, aby zachować sens zdania wyjściowego. Konieczna jest pełna poprawność gramatyczna i ortograficzna wpisywanych fraz.

__________ for our goalkeeper, we would have lost the match 0-5.
The winners of the competition __________ next Monday.
Do you know anyone __________ can fix a broken laptop?
My grandpa has a very __________ sense of humour: he tells jokes with a completely serious face.
Please __________ in mind that the museum closes at five o'clock.
Stop __________ around the bush and tell me what really happened!
I can't __________ out what this sign says: the letters are too small.
It was the __________ interesting museum I have ever visited: I was bored the whole time.
Kasia is __________ the cleverest person in our class: nobody else even comes close.
I'll write your phone number down __________ I forget it.
Not only __________ the cake, but she also made all the decorations.
I __________ this book for weeks, and I'm still only on page 50.
I have two older brothers, __________ are at university now.
Can you __________ the table for dinner, please? The plates are in the cupboard.
When the last exam was over, we all __________ a sigh of relief.
My cousin and I look so alike that people say we're like two __________ in a pod.
Let's __________ off early tomorrow so we don't get stuck in traffic.
This year's school show was every __________ as good as last year's.
The film was nearly three hours long. __________, I wasn't bored for a single minute.
If you __________ me, I would have helped you with your project.
Nobody phoned while I was out, __________?
My bike, __________ I got for my tenth birthday, is still as good as new.
Not __________ what to say, I just smiled and nodded.
My uncle __________ a living by repairing old bikes.
It's __________ to say that our class has the best football team in the school.
I've said I'm sorry, so now the ball is in your __________.
We need to __________ up with a name for our band before the concert.
Kraków is the __________ biggest city in Poland, after Warsaw.
__________ it was raining, we decided to stay at home and play board games.
I wish it __________ raining: I want to go to the park!
Everything __________ he told us turned out to be true.
My little brother keeps __________ my pens without asking!
The shop is closed, so we might as __________ go home.

tasks.instruction: Odpowiedz na pytania wybierając jedną poprawną odpowiedź z zaproponowanych możliwości A) – D).

items.question: What nickname is often used for the Conservative Party and its members?
What is the last step before a bill passed by both Houses of Parliament becomes law?
options: D. the State Opening of Parliament

items.question: At which London address did Sherlock Holmes live in Arthur Conan Doyle's stories?
Which event took place in Hyde Park in 1851?
options: A. the coronation of Queen Victoria
B. the first modern Olympic Games
C. the opening of the first Underground line
D. the Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace

items.question: Which is the oldest part of the Tower of London, begun by William the Conqueror?
In which year was the cross of St Patrick added to the Union Flag?
When do people in England celebrate St George's Day?
Who writes the King's Speech that the King reads at the State Opening of Parliament?
options: B. the Speaker of the House of Commons

items.question: In which language was the Magna Carta written?
On which islands did Charles Darwin notice that the finches and tortoises were slightly different on each island?
Which king joined the white rose of York and the red rose of Lancaster into the Tudor rose?
What is the name of the building where the Scottish Parliament meets?
What do people in Argentina call the Falkland Islands?
Which scientist designed the Monument together with Sir Christopher Wren?
Who was born in Kensington Palace?
Which king burst into the House of Commons in 1642 to arrest five MPs, which is why the door is slammed in Black Rod's face at the State Opening?
Which party was founded in 1900 by trade unions and socialist groups to represent working people?
Why is the Royal Standard never flown at half-mast, even when a monarch dies?
options: A. There is always a monarch: the next one reigns from the moment the last one dies.
B. It is flown only on the monarch's birthday.
C. By law, only the Union Flag may be flown at half-mast.
D. It is too large to be lowered halfway.

items.question: Which Prime Minister resigned in January 1957 after the Suez Crisis?
Where is Charles Darwin buried?
Who was the last monarch to refuse Royal Assent to a bill passed by Parliament?
Which Prime Minister's government created the NHS (National Health Service) in 1948?
According to a legend, how did the thistle help Scotland?
options: A. St Andrew planted thistles around Edinburgh Castle to keep enemies out.
B. Barefoot Viking attackers stepped on thistles and cried out, which woke the Scots.
C. Scottish soldiers ate thistles to survive a long winter siege.
D. A thistle grew where the first King of Scotland was crowned.

items.question: Which queen was beheaded at the Tower of London in 1536?
What does the golden statue of Prince Albert in the Albert Memorial hold?
options: C. a map of the British Empire
D. the catalogue of the Great Exhibition

items.question: Why do the Yeomen of the Guard search the cellars of the Palace of Westminster before the State Opening of Parliament?
options: A. to find the Mace, which is locked away in the cellars overnight
B. because of a tradition going back to 1605, when Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament
C. to check that the King's carriage, which is kept down there, is ready
D. to make sure that no MP is hiding there to miss the King's Speech

items.question: Which of these is decided by the UK Parliament in Westminster for the whole country, and not by the Scottish Parliament?
Who described the Great Fire of London in his famous diary, and even buried his cheese to save it from the flames?
In which year did women in the UK get the vote on the same terms as men?
Why is the motto on the Royal Coat of Arms, 'Dieu et mon droit', in French?
options: A. It was a gift to an English king from a king of France.
B. The first coat of arms was made in Paris.
C. A French artist designed it for Queen Victoria.
D. English kings spoke French for centuries after the Norman Conquest of 1066.

items.question: Who runs the debates in the House of Commons and calls 'Order! Order!' when MPs get too noisy?
Which country of the UK has no parliament or assembly of its own, so its laws are made by the UK Parliament?
Why is the flag of Scotland a white X on a blue background?
options: A. The X stands for ten, the number of the old Scottish kingdoms.
B. St Andrew was killed on an X-shaped cross.
C. It shows the two swords of a famous Scottish king.
D. It was copied from the flag of the Viking attackers.

items.question: What is on top of the Monument, the column built to remember the Great Fire of London?
options: A. a statue of Sir Christopher Wren
C. a golden urn with flames

items.question: What is the Serpentine in Hyde Park?
options: A. a glass building from the Great Exhibition
B. a long lake made in the 18th century
C. a winding path for horse riders
D. a very old oak tree
